Commentary.Commentary: We are back. The covers were on during the break but it has been removed now. The players are out in the middle doing their drills. All set now. Sediqullah Atal and Abdul Malik to open for Afghanistan. Blessing Muzarabani to bowl first.
...Second innings...

Afghanistan might be relieved by rattling the hosts but there's still a lot of work left for them. They stuck with spinners for most part of the innings. AM Ghazanfar on his debut took three wickets while Zadran, Khan and Zia-ur-Rehman ended with two each. Zimbabwe bowlers will be fresh and raring to go. They'll hope for a couple of quick wickets before the end of the day's play. Afghanistan on the other hand need a good start. Stay tuned.

Finally, the innings comes to an end but a show Zimbabwe have put on! They have dominated the game so far and have the upper hand. It was all about three centurions for Zimbabwe. Their experienced players, Sean Williams, Craig Ervine and Brian Bennett stepped up to the occasion. The trio played brilliantly in different phases to score such a massive score. Earlier, the debutant, Curran notched a fifty and there were a couple of handy innings from Myers and Newman Nyamhuri as well.

Well, Afghanistan were too eager for a wicket and in the process were not able to bowl two consecutive good deliveries. They were just not able to build pressure and in return gave plenty of freebies to the hosts. Hashmatullah Shahidi shuffled his bowling option, mainly going with spinners but didn't get much success in return. Afghanistan looked tired eventually. They'll hope the new day will bring some energy as Afghanistan could take this score well over 500 if they don't take wickets. Join us for the action of Day 2 at 8 am GMT. Till then, cheers!

A fantastic day for the hosts! They have started really well in the series. Zimbabwe opted to bat first on a sunny Boxing Day morning. Ben Curran was at the thick of action as on his debut he took the attack and scored a fine fifty. He fell in the final over before Lunch but Zimbabwe stitch another big partnership with Takudzwanashe Kaitano and Sean Williams. The former fell but Williams is still going strong, unbeaten on 145. He along with the skipper have bossed the final session and have taken the upper hand in this game on Day 1.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back!
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

Afghanistan haven't been at their best in the field! The bowling hasn't been very disciplined too and they'll hope to do better after the break. There isn't much on offer from the wicket but they'll hope this wicket opens the floodgates. An important session awaits. Do join us after the break.

That wicket right at the end will make Afghanistan feel a lot better but Zimbabwe have done really well in this session! Their openers got them off to a good start before that stand was broken and then the 2nd wicket partnership continued the good work. Ben Curran looked in fine touch and he was the star. Just as it seemed they would enter the break only one down, AM Ghazanfar struck and got the better of Curran. Still though, Zimbabwe are in a decent position and they'll hope to continue the good work after the break!

OUT! BOWLED! Curran goes in the final over before Lunch! AM Ghazanfar gets a wicket on his debut! Flighted full and on middle and leg. Curran leans to defend but it goes through the gate and hits the stumps. LUNCH!

Afghanistan will again be the favourites in the Test series as they have retained most of the squads and have players in red-hot form. Zimbabwe on the other hand have experience on their side but need their senior players to step up to the occasion. Zimbabwe though have a chance to redeem themselves in the longest format of the game as they'll host the Boxing Day Test for the first time ever at home in 28 years. They have played cricket below their standards so far but they'll hope the Christmas break could bring some positive air in their camp and fire under their belly to win the Test series.
